featured_reviews.review_text:
Visit to the Gaushala – A Peaceful and Heartwarming Experience

One of the best places to visit for peace, kindness, and a connection with nature is the Gaushala. This is not just a shelter for cows, but a sanctuary where love for animals comes to life. When you visit the Gaushala, you can offer ghaas (grass) and laddoos to the cows, chana aur bajra to the pigeons, and food to other animal . It’s a soothing and satisfying experience for all ages.

The atmosphere is calm and spiritual. Children and adults alike enjoy feeding the animals and feeling close to them. You can also buy fresh cow milk, known for its purity and health benefits. Many people come here regularly to buy milk directly from the source.

The visiting hours are:

Morning: 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM

Evening: 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM

Another beautiful aspect of the Gaushala is the chance to make a donation to support the care and feeding of the animals. Whether it’s a small amount or a regular contribution, your help makes a big difference.

featured_reviews.name: D Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Heartfelt Thank You to TATF & Deepa

As many of our friends know, 2023 didn’t end gently for us. It was a time filled with grief, long days, and sleepless nights.

But in that silence, we realized we might need someone to help us through.

Not something impulsive, not a rushed decision, just an unspoken understanding between the two of us that perhaps the love we had to give wasn’t meant to stop.

And that’s when fate stepped in.

While scrolling through Instagram one night, I came across The Anubis-Tiger Foundation. Something nudged me to send a message, just putting it out there that we were open to welcoming a pup in need of a home.

I didn’t expect a reply so soon. But within a few hours, Deepa reached out - with a photo of an angel who, as it turned out, was waiting for us too.

The moment we saw her, we just knew.
She was ours. And we were hers.

Despite everything, I never imagined it would all happen so quickly. But perhaps that’s because I hadn’t realized just how many people are out there giving up their pets, sometimes for heartbreaking reasons. It left me sad, confused, and questioning how anyone could let go of such love.

But I’ll be honest - we’re also thankful.

Because if that family hadn’t made their decision, we would’ve never met Aura.

On 21st January 2024, we brought her home. We braced ourselves, thinking she might take time to adjust after a year with her previous family.

But Aura had other plans.

Within a day, she chose us - just as we had chosen her. She knew she was home.

She changed everything. The energy, the silence, the air itself. And her name came so naturally: Aura.

We went into this thinking we were rescuing her. But in truth, she rescued us.

We are so grateful to have her in our lives.

Thank you, Deepa, you who don’t just find homes for these beautiful souls, but make sure they find the right ones.

She doesn’t hand them over to just anyone. She takes the time to check, to understand, and to ensure that the home is one filled with the love, care, and stability every animal deserves.

Thank you, Anubis Foundation.
And thank you to the angel above who showed us the way.

❤️

featured_reviews.review_text: I had few cats neutered with this NGO. Good thing is that they are good at surgery. Bad thing. The staff never picks up call or responds to your concerns about the cat. As a caretaker, we are concerned for our cats health especially if they are at a new place. As an NGO they should understand and inculcate in this behaviour. Swapna is too rude and arrogant. She should improve her behaviour and talking skills with people. You are not doing any favour on your customers. In facts customer favours you. This attitude won’t go long way. However she’s compassionate towards animals. As a lawyer, I understand the challenges faced by an NGO, but it never provides you a leeway to behave badly.

featured_reviews.name: Mohsin Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took my cat, Panda, to All About Them for neutering. She was a tuxedo cat. I was charged ₹2,500 for the procedure, which included post-operative care. However, when I brought her home after she stayed at their clinic for two days following the surgery, she seemed extremely lethargic.

Fifteen days after bringing her back, she suddenly fell very ill and had difficulty walking. I rushed her to the hospital, where the vet mentioned that she might have contracted a viral infection from being in a place with many other cats. When I informed the doctor that she had been neutered and had stayed at All About Them for two days, he confirmed that it was possible she had picked up the infection there.

Unfortunately, despite receiving multiple injections and fluids, she couldn’t recover and sadly passed away the same day. I don’t directly blame All About Them, but I am deeply disappointed because they assured me that the cats would be well cared for during post-op recovery. Had I known that infections were a risk at their facility, I would have taken her home immediately after the surgery instead.

review_photos.caption: This was her condition before she passed away.
She was unable to walk and breathe

customer_updates.name: Vijay Patil
customer_updates.text:
ज़रूरी सूचना / Urgent Notice
हिन्दी:
नमस्ते,
मैंने एक कुत्ते को देखा है जिसे तुरंत मदद की ज़रूरत है।
कुत्ते की स्थिति:
* वह बीमार दिख रहा है।
* वह अस्वाभाविक रूप से व्यवहार कर रहा था (मेरे पीछे आ रहा था, दूसरे कुत्तों पर हमला कर रहा था)।
* उसके मुँह से लार या झाग निकल रहा था।
* वह बहुत आक्रामक लग रहा था।
कृपया जल्द से जल्द इसकी मदद करें।
धन्यवाद।
English:
Hello,
I have seen a dog that urgently needs help.
Dog's Condition:
* It appears to be sick.
* It was behaving unusually (following me, attacking other dogs).
* There was saliva or foam coming from its mouth.
* It seemed very aggressive.
Please provide assistance as soon as possible.
Thank you.
मराठी:
नमस्कार,
मला एक कुत्रा दिसला आहे ज्याला त्वरित मदतीची गरज आहे.
कुत्र्याची स्थिती:
* तो आजारी दिसत आहे.
* तो असामान्यपणे वागत होता (माझ्या मागे येत होता, इतर कुत्र्यांवर हल्ला करत होता).
* त्याच्या तोंडातून लाळ किंवा फेस बाहेर येत होता.
* तो खूप आक्रमक वाटत होता.
कृपया लवकरच याला मदत करा.
धन्यवाद.

I do NOT recommend this rescue service at all.
I found a small puppy on the road and took care of him for almost a month with proper food and attention. Trusting them, I handed him over for rescue, as they assured me of proper care, checkup, and vaccination.
However, after they took the puppy, they completely stopped answering calls and messages. When we personally visited their location later, we were shocked to see the puppy’s condition had become much worse. There was no proper care, no medical treatment, and no vaccination as promised.
This is extremely irresponsible and heartbreaking. Please do not trust them with any animal’s life. Animals deserve love and proper care, not neglect like this.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This NGO truly sets a gold standard in social service. Their team is upfront, proactive, and available 24×7, which is rare and incredibly reassuring. No matter the time or situation, they step in immediately and take responsibility rather than making excuses.

What really stands out is their willingness to go the extra mile—sometimes even beyond what is expected or required—to ensure real help reaches those in need. Their work is driven by compassion, transparency, and action, not just words.

It’s organizations like this that restore faith in humanity. Deep respect and gratitude to the entire team for their tireless dedication and selfless service. Highly recommended and truly trustworthy. 🌟

featured_reviews.name: dhiraj tiwari
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are moments in life when help is needed not tomorrow, not in the morning—but right now. This NGO was a true lifesaver for me at midnight, when I had almost lost hope. They didn’t just respond quickly; they responded with genuine care, empathy, and respect.

A very special mention to Bhavesh, the real protagonist who stepped in and treated me with incredible hospitality and kindness. He made sure I felt safe, supported, and heard—something you never forget in times of distress.

This organization doesn’t just “help” people; they stand by you when it matters most. If you’re ever in need or looking to support an NGO that truly makes a difference on the ground, I wholeheartedly recommend them. Eternal gratitude 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Manisha Pal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I met Mr mohan he is very helpful...
He saved 2 kitties from our area came for immediate assistance formalities were very smooth.. one of the best organisation for animal rescue and adoption center..

featured_reviews.name: Khushi Kachalia
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a stray kitten that no one was willing to adopt, her mom had died and we just picked her up off the street with no knowledge of how to care for her. We couldn't keep her because we could not transport her back to our home, and we already had a dog. She had fleas and worms and we were terrified about what to do for her. We called ARAS in the morning and they got back to us immediately and in the next 2-3 hours the founder came to pick her up. He even explained that you may video call the foundation or request pictures to check in on the animal. The work these people are doing is incredible, and the complaints about the request for donations is completely unjustified. Pets are expensive, these people are paying rent for a property as well as feeding, grooming, and giving medical care to over some 60 animals. A big thank you to Bhavesh Jain and everyone else working for this foundation ! As for Ginger, I hope someone will adopt her, she's very sweet, loves to cuddle and only 1.5-2 months old. There are pictures of her below, and if you are interested go ahead and give this number a call. 😄

name: Youth Organisation In Defence Of Animals
description:
Established in 2011 by four individuals united by their deep love for animals and their commitment to making a difference. As a socially responsible organization, YODA activey supports animals through a variety of impactful initiatives, including:
- Operating 3 rehabilitation centres in Malad, Khar & Goa.
- Providing free treatment and emergency services.
- Conducting sterilisations, vaccinations, and specialised surgeries.
- Facilitating adoptions for street and abandoned animals.
- Promoting education, awareness, and coexistence.

featured_reviews.name: Daya Sansare
featured_reviews.review_text: Wonderful experience! The people there were very helpful and calm. My pet cat was properly being taken care of. Would definitely recommend anyone looking to neuter their cat, it would be great.

featured_reviews.name: nitin s
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently got my cat spayed at Yoda Animal Shelter, and I had a really positive experience. The entire process was handled professionally and with genuine care for the animals.
A special thanks to Roshni, the manager, who was extremely supportive throughout. She patiently explained everything and provided clear, practical after-care instructions, which made the recovery process much easier for me and my cat.
It’s reassuring to see such dedication and compassion towards animal welfare. I would definitely recommend Yoda Animal Shelter to anyone looking for trustworthy and caring veterinary support.

featured_reviews.name: Rahat FreeSpirit
featured_reviews.review_text: Good place for rescuers. Treatment might delay due to excessive crowd and load that the team bears. They helped one of my stray dog in operting  with broken hip joint, he recovered very well . I am greatful for whatever best they are doing. During lockdown Yoda had provided food for strays . God bless the Max and Yoda team 🙏🐾

featured_reviews.name: Ninochkha Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this place for a philanthropic event organised by my workplace... At the beginning it looked like a task to do so many chores..then starting with the work and those cute little faces melted my heart ❤️❤️
The cats and dogs were so friendly .. and were so excited to see and play with us ...

I would recommend you guys to have a visit and spend some time with these little angels

featured_reviews.name: GM Lotlikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am totally disappointed and heartbroken with my experience at Yoda NGO situated at Malad Chikuwadi. I had sent my cat for sterilization and kept following up from day one, but my messages and calls were continuously ignored. Despite my repeated requests for updates, I wasn’t informed about my cat’s condition or whereabouts.

After 15 days of constant follow-ups, I was shocked to learn that my cat had been released five days earlier without any prior intimation or confirmation from me. To make things worse, my cat was left without my permission in a location that is extremely difficult to find. This is extremely irresponsible and careless behavior.

Animals are not just “cases” they are family. My cat was like my baby.  I had some emotional sentiments connection with my cat. NGOs like Yoda are expected to show compassion, transparency, and accountability, not negligence. What happened to my cat should never happen to anyone else.

Please, if you truly care for animals, think twice before trusting this organization with your pets.

#AnimalWelfare #AccountabilityMatters #YodaNGO #AnimalCare

featured_reviews.name: S Muskan
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Yoda Malad in June and had a really unpleasant experience with the manager, Tanya. She was surprisingly rude and dismissive and loud, which made the whole visit uncomfortable. I had gone there with good intentions to enquire about sterilization and other queries, but after that encounter, I honestly wouldn’t go back.  Really disappointing experience. Wouldn't recommend this place to anyone looking to help community animals for free.

featured_reviews.name: Mukesh Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text: I have visited for the first time in yoda. I have gone there with My cat, and there were many cats and dogs, they have rescued them, and the pet animals of youth organisations, are very friendly with us. The medical facilities are free of cost. It was a best experience in youth organisations defence of animals..😊

featured_reviews.name: sweety chougule
featured_reviews.review_text:
I want to give a huge Thank you to YODA for the wonderful work they do. I recently sent my 3 community female dogs for spaying.
The team was gentle, patient and very reassuring throughout the process. Their team truly cares, from handling the pups gently to keeping us updated and making sure they are safe and comfortable. I’m so grateful for the effort they put in every single day for so many strays.
Thank you for making a difference and taking such good of our furry babies♥️ 🐾

featured_reviews.name: Sanjay Borade
featured_reviews.review_text: We recently had a snake spotted in our society late at night, and the Hope Foundation team responded immediately when we contacted them at midnight. They arrived quickly, handled the situation very professionally, and safely rescued the snake with proper care and expertise. Truly grateful for their fast response and dedication to both people and wildlife. Thank you, Hope Foundation, for your amazing work!

featured_reviews.name: Yash Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was trying to get a street dog admited. He has bot flies all over, he was walking in circles and almost a skeleton. He was not eating anything.

They told me they don't take animals with ticks, fleas, or botflies. As it would "spread to other animals".... You are literally an animal clinic and rescue organisation. It's your job to look after the sick and isolate to animal with contagious condition. They are actively declining animals with most common aliment.

So what, you only take animals with lavish background? All streets animals have some sort of fleas and ticks. It's like human hospital not talking anyone with common cold as it would spread to others.

As I was trying to point out the absurdity of the whole thing. She got mad.

featured_reviews.name: Sanya Bahadur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last year I had rescued an indie cat named Cheese from the streets and due to family issues, could'nt adopt him. We immediately called Hope Foundation for foster care services and since then, Rohitji & his wife have been taking very good care of Cheese👍

They have informed me from time to time about his medical issues, shared his updates and taken care of him when he fell sick. Cheese too is very happy with them.

Hope Foundation was my last hope to ensure that Cheese gets to live a sheltered life, safely and away from the streets. And I will always remain grateful to them for helping both me & Cheese at our time of need🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Chaitali Salvi
featured_reviews.review_text: Our society cat Boku was badly injured. Even the animal hospital and ambulance refused help over the long weekend, saying no doctors were available, but Hope Foundation stepped in immediately. They not only responded quickly, but also took such good care of him, and ensured us he was looked after with love. The team was extremely cooperative, gave us regular updates, and their compassion truly made a difference. We are deeply grateful for your support.

featured_reviews.name: Sumeet Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Came across a dehydrated Black Kite one evening in my society and called them for rescue.
Rohit Khuranna and his team handled it in professional manner and you could see the love and dedication that they put forth.
So grateful this foundation exists - definitely worth supporting them 💯💯.

featured_reviews.name: Ashween Menda
featured_reviews.review_text:
We called for snake at home at Mamta, opp Santosh mata mandir.

call reply and instant help in minites.
They took the snake safely.
Truly thankful.

featured_reviews.name: Saumya Chaudhary
featured_reviews.review_text:
I called them for urgent help for a dog in my neighbourhood, and all they cared about was money. The entire conversation revolved around payment, not the suffering animal. Eventually, help was flat out denied. One woman I spoke to was outright dismissive and refused to do anything.
If your only motive is to make money, don’t hide behind the label of an NGO. Turning away helpless animals while preaching “welfare” is shameful. This organisation should seriously question its ethics. Absolutely disgraceful.
